patients.summary: Retired math teacher with a 2013 mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3a and hyperlipidemia who joins in 2022 just before a right hip replacement. The hip later becomes chronically infected and is treated with a two-stage exchange; severe aortic stenosis, tap-responsive normal pressure hydrocephalus (shunted) and recurrent bleeding from cecal angiodysplasia with iron deficiency follow. Today a capsule endoscopy is booked and the aortic stenosis has never been taken to intervention.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 72 y/o retired HS math teacher, transferring care from a practice he'd been with for years. Main reason for coming: wants one doctor who will run his warfarin and see the whole picture.

HPI: Mechanical mitral valve placed in 2013. Has been on warfarin since, goal INR 2.5-3.5, on 5 mg nightly with occasional adjustments; last INRs at his old office in range per his log book, no bleeding or clot history he knows of. Also takes aspirin 81. HTN on lisinopril 20 and amlodipine 5, home readings he says are 'in the 120s.' DM2 for about ten years on metformin 1000 BID, last A1c 'just under 7.' Statin for lipids. Told his kidneys are 'stage 3, stable' for a few years. Constipation is long-standing, uses an OTC stool softener every so often, not bothersome. Colonoscopy spring 2021 with polyps removed, told 3 years.

Right hip: years of worsening pain, severe arthritis on x-ray per his surgeon, now limping and using the banister on stairs. Right total hip is booked for 9/27. He'll need a bridging plan for the warfarin, which is part of why he wanted to get established now.

PMH/PSH: as above. Mechanical MVR 2013. Polypectomy 2021.
Meds: warfarin 5 mg qhs, lisinopril 20 daily, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40 daily, amlodipine 5 daily, ASA 81 daily, docusate prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family hx: no colon cancer in the family, no early heart disease, nobody with HHT that he knows of.
Social: retired from teaching high school math. Quit smoking 2007, about 20 pack-years before that. Wine 1-2 glasses a week. Walks less than he'd like because of the hip.

ROS: neg for chest pain, palpitations, syncope, bleeding, black stools, urinary sx. Hip as above.

Exam: Well-appearing, pleasant. Vitals reviewed. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no JVD. Heart: regular rhythm, crisp mechanical valve click. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT, no masses. Ext no edema. Right hip with painful, limited internal rotation; antalgic gait. Feet: intact sensation to monofilament, pulses palpable, no lesions.

PHQ-2 negative.

A/P:
1. Mechanical mitral valve on warfarin - we'll take over INR management. INR today. Continue 5 mg nightly. ASA 81 continued.
2. Right hip OA, THA 9/27 - preop visit ~2 wks before surgery; will set up warfarin hold with enoxaparin bridge then.
3. HTN - at goal, no change.
4. DM2 - A1c, UACR today. Continue metformin. Eye exam due, he'll book with his optometrist.
5. CKD 3a - CMP today, keep off NSAIDs (he knows).
6. HLD - lipids.
7. Hx polyps - surveillance due ~2024.
8. Records requested from prior office.

RTC for preop mid-Sept.

OUTSIDE ORTHOPEDIC SURGERY GROUP - CLINIC NOTE
Date of service: 01/25/2023

Reason: right hip pain, low-grade fevers, s/p right THA 09/27/2022.

History: Mr. Graves is about four months out from his right total hip. He did well at first but over the past several weeks has developed a constant, dull ache in the right hip that now limits how far he can walk. He has had low-grade temperatures and some night sweats. He denies any fall or injury. His PCP saw him in November for warfarin monitoring of his mechanical mitral valve, at which time the hip was improving.

PMH: mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, HTN, DM2, hyperlipidemia, CKD 3, chronic constipation, history of colon polyps.
Meds: warfarin, lisinopril, metformin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, aspirin 81.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Afebrile in clinic. Right hip incision well healed. The skin over the hip is not red or warm. Tender to palpation around the prosthesis. ROM limited by pain in all planes. Distal neurovascular exam intact.

X-rays right hip: components in good position, no fracture, no dislocation.

Labs today: WBC 9.0, ESR 55, CRP 25 mg/L. Blood cultures drawn - no growth so far.

Procedure: Right hip aspiration under sterile technique. Synovial fluid: WBC 3,500/uL, 65% neutrophils. Gram stain - no organisms. Culture sent.

Assessment: Right hip pain with elevated inflammatory markers and an abnormal synovial cell count four months after arthroplasty - chronic periprosthetic joint infection until proven otherwise. Await culture.

Plan: We will call with the culture. Likely a staged revision. Infectious disease referral to follow. Will coordinate warfarin management with his PCP.

Right hip aspirate culture from 01/25: Staphylococcus epidermidis, oxacillin-resistant, vancomycin-susceptible. Blood cultures no growth.

Recommended two-stage exchange: first stage removal of the implant and placement of an antibiotic cement spacer, then 6 weeks of IV antibiotics, then reimplantation once infection markers settle. INFECTIOUS DISEASE CONSULTATION
Date of service: 02/03/2023
Referred by: orthopedic surgery

72M with mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, DM2, CKD 3a, right THA 9/2022, now with chronic PJI of the right hip. Aspirate 1/25 grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, oxacillin-resistant, vancomycin-susceptible. Blood cultures negative. No murmur of concern on my exam beyond his prosthetic valve sounds; given negative blood cultures and no embolic signs I don't think he needs an echo for endocarditis at this time.

Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: T 37.2. Well-appearing. Mechanical click. Right hip tender, no sinus tract.

Impression: Chronic periprosthetic infection of the right hip due to methicillin-resistant S. epidermidis.

Recommendations:
1. Agree with two-stage exchange.
2. After stage 1, IV vancomycin dosed by pharmacy to trough 15-20, anticipate 1,250 mg q24h given his kidney function, for 6 weeks from the date of surgery via PICC with home infusion.
3. Weekly CBC, BMP and vancomycin trough while on therapy; copies to PCP, who manages his INR.
4. Off antibiotics at least 2 weeks before reimplantation, with ESR/CRP before stage 2.
5. Follow up in ID clinic at end of therapy.

reports.text:
Indication: dyspnea on exertion, systolic murmur, mechanical mitral valve.
Left ventricle: normal size. Mildly reduced systolic function, LVEF 48% by biplane Simpson. No regional wall motion abnormality.
Aortic valve: trileaflet, heavily calcified with restricted leaflet motion. Aortic valve area 0.8 cm2 by continuity. Mean gradient 50 mmHg. No significant aortic regurgitation.
Mitral valve: mechanical prosthesis, well seated, normal leaflet motion and normal transmitral gradient for prosthesis type; no paravalvular leak.
Right ventricle: normal size and function.
Atria: normal size.
Pericardium: no effusion.
IVC normal size with normal respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: Severe calcific aortic stenosis (AVA 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 50 mmHg). LVEF 48%. Normally functioning mechanical mitral prosthesis.

documents.title: Capsule test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The GI office sent the instructions for the camera pill in September. It says to stop iron 3 days before but doesn't say anything about the warfarin. Do I need the shots again like last time? My daughter is asking. - Bob

documents.title: RE: Capsule test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. No - the capsule is just swallowed, nothing is cut or removed, so keep taking warfarin as usual and no injections this time. Do stop the iron 3 days before as they asked, and restart it the day after. Also, with the capsule in you shouldn't have an MRI until it has passed - and your shunt valve needs a check after any MRI anyway. Call with any other questions.
